title: Alternating horn filtration of the walking-isomorphism nerve
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal J$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism for each ordered pair, put $J=N(\mathcal J)$, and let $i:\Delta^1\hookrightarrow J$ be the nerve of the functor selecting $0\to1$. There are simplicial subsets $J_1\subseteq J_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J$ whose union is $J$, with $J_1=i(\Delta^1)$, such that for every $n\geq2$ the inclusion $J_{n-1}\hookrightarrow J_n$ is (up to the displayed identifications) a pushout of the horn inclusion $\Lambda^n_0\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. More explicitly, the new nondegenerate simplices at stage $n$ are the alternating word $w_n=(0,1,0,\ldots)$ and its face $d_0w_n=(1,0,1,\ldots)$; every other proper face of these simplices already lies in $J_{n-1}$. The same construction with the initial vertex $1$ gives the reversed filtration.

source.place: Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1 and Remark 3.1.2.6; the alternating-word filtration is an agent-written expansion of the horn attachment for this nerve. Online source read 2026-10-17; WANTED archival copy.

proof.text: By the nerve description in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $r$-simplex of $J=N(\mathcal J)$ is a word $(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ with each $x_j\in\{0,1\}$, since between every ordered pair of objects there is exactly one morphism. Such a simplex is degenerate exactly when some consecutive pair is equal: a degeneracy repeats a vertex, and conversely a repeated adjacent vertex is the image of the word with that repetition deleted. Therefore the nondegenerate $r$-simplices are precisely the two alternating words $w_r^0=(0,1,0,\ldots)$ and $w_r^1=(1,0,1,\ldots)$ (with the evident interpretation in dimensions $0$ and $1$).

source.place: Word description of the nerve and its degenerate simplices. Agent-written from the nerve and horn clauses of def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones; Kerodon tag 00UG (Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1, anodyne morphisms as the weakly saturated closure of horns) is the context in which the filtration is used, not a statement of this step.

proof.text: Let $J_1$ be the simplicial subset generated by the vertices and the edge $0\to1$, and for $n\geq2$ let $J_n$ be the simplicial subset generated by $J_1$ together with $w_m^0$ for $2\leq m\leq n$. For an alternating word, deleting an interior vertex creates two equal adjacent vertices, so $d_jw_m^0$ is degenerate for $0<j<m$. The last face is $d_mw_m^0=w_{m-1}^0$, while the first face is $d_0w_m^0=w_{m-1}^1$. Hence, relative to $J_{m-1}$, the only new nondegenerate simplices contributed by $w_m^0$ and its faces are $w_m^0$ and $d_0w_m^0$; every other proper face already belongs to $J_{m-1}$. This also shows the inclusions $J_{m-1}\subseteq J_m$ are well defined.

source.place: Alternating-word face calculation. Agent-written from the nerve and horn clauses of def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones; Kerodon tag 00UG (Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1, anodyne morphisms as the weakly saturated closure of horns) is the context in which the filtration is used, not a statement of this step.

proof.text: The face calculation gives the pushout description. Map the horn $\Lambda_0^n$ to $J_{n-1}$ by restricting the map $\sigma:\Delta^n\to J$ classified by $w_n^0$; this lands in $J_{n-1}$ because the horn is the union of the faces other than the $0$th by the horn definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and by Step 2 those faces $d_jw_n^0$, $j\neq0$, lie in $J_{n-1}$. Form the degreewise pushout $P_n=J_{n-1}\amalg_{\Lambda_0^n}\Delta^n$; since $\Lambda_0^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is injective, $(P_n)_m=(J_{n-1})_m\sqcup((\Delta^n)_m\setminus(\Lambda_0^n)_m)$. By the horn definition, an $m$-simplex $f:[m]\to[n]$ of $\Delta^n$ lies outside $\Lambda_0^n$ exactly when its image contains $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its image $\sigma(f)=(x_{f(0)},\ldots,x_{f(m)})$, with $w_n^0=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, is the word whose maximal constant runs have the lengths $|f^{-1}(k)|$ for $k$ in the image of $f$: it has $n+1$ runs beginning with $0$ if $f$ is surjective and $n$ runs beginning with $1$ if the image is $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The word therefore determines $f$, so $\sigma$ is injective on these simplices. Collapsing its runs gives $w_n^0$ or $w_{n-1}^1$ respectively. By Step 1 a simplex of $J$ is the degeneracy of the nondegenerate word obtained by collapsing its runs, and a simplex lies in $J_{n-1}$ only if that collapsed word does. By Step 2 the nondegenerate simplices of $J_{n-1}$ are $w_k^0$ for $k\leq n-1$ and $w_k^1$ for $k\leq n-2$, so these images are not in $J_{n-1}$. They are exactly the simplices of $J_n$ not in $J_{n-1}$, namely the degeneracies of the two new nondegenerate simplices $w_n^0$ and $d_0w_n^0=w_{n-1}^1$. Hence the canonical map $P_n\to J_n$ is a degreewise bijection, so it is an isomorphism of simplicial sets, and $J_{n-1}\hookrightarrow J_n$ is the asserted pushout of $\Lambda_0^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$.

source.place: Degreewise horn pushout for the stage inclusion. Agent-written from the nerve and horn clauses of def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones; Kerodon tag 00UG (Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1, anodyne morphisms as the weakly saturated closure of horns) is the context in which the filtration is used, not a statement of this step.

proof.text: The nerve of the functor $[1]\to\mathcal J$ selecting $0\to1$ is exactly $J_1$, so $J_1=i(\Delta^1)$. Every $w_n^0$ lies in $J_n$, and every opposite alternating word $w_n^1$ is $d_0w_{n+1}^0$ and therefore lies in $J_{n+1}$. Step 1 then implies that every simplex of $J$ is in some $J_n$, because every degenerate simplex is a degeneracy of a nondegenerate one. Hence $\bigcup_nJ_n=J$. Interchanging the labels $0$ and $1$ gives the same construction beginning with the edge $1\to0$, which is the reversed filtration. The cases $n=0,1$ and the empty degeneracy faces are included in these formulas.
